Other Branches of Social Sciences Outside Class H

  • Political Science (Class J): Covers political theory, legislative bodies, and international relations. [2, 3]
  • Law (Class K): Covers regional, national, and international legal systems. [2, 3]
  • Education (Class L): Covers the theory, practice, and history of education. [2, 3]
  • Anthropology & Geography (Class G):
    • G–GF: Geography (Physical, Human, and Cultural)
    • GN: Anthropology & Ethnology [2, 4]
  • Psychology (Class B): Specifically housed under Subclass BF (within Philosophy, Psychology, and Religion). [2, 5]
  • History (Classes C, D, E, F):
    • C: Auxiliary Sciences of History (Archeology, Genealogy, Numismatics)
    • D: World History (Old World, Europe, Asia, Africa)
    • E–F: History of the Americas & United States [2, 3]
  • Linguistics (Class P): Housed under Subclass P (Philology and Linguistics general). [2]

title: Cultural
content:
🏛️ 1. Culture & Way of Life (Broad Overview)
Books exploring culture from an anthropological or sociological lens are classified under the 300 Social Sciences main class. [3, 4]
  • 306 Culture and Institutions: This is the core classification for general books on culture, mass media, popular culture, and cultural anthropology.
  • 306.09: Historical and geographical treatment of specific cultures or civilizations. [4]

👥 2. Social Habits, Customs & Etiquette

Daily traditions, folkways, and societal behaviors are separated from general sociology and given their own dedicated division. [3]
  • 390 Customs, Etiquette, Folklore: The main home for ancestral traditions and societal manners.
  • 391 Costume and Personal Appearance: Cultural dress, fashion history, and body ornamentation.
  • 392 Customs of Life Cycle & Domestic Life: Rituals surrounding birth, coming-of-age, marriage, and family structures.
  • 394 General Customs: Holidays, seasonal festivals, dining/food habits, and public celebrations.
  • 395 Etiquette: Rules of social politeness and manners across different societies. [1, 3, 5]

🎨 3. The Arts & Creative Expression

When looking at culture through its artistic output, materials shift completely into the 700s and 800s. [6]
  • 700 The Arts & Recreation: The main class for creative and fine arts.
  • 720 Architecture: Cultural building styles and historic structures.
  • 730–760 Visual Arts: Sculpture, ceramics, textiles, and painting.
  • 780 Music: Traditional folk music, instruments, and cultural audio expressions.
  • 790 Performing Arts: Cultural dance, theater, and traditional games.
  • 800 Literature: Poems, plays, folklore, and stories written by a specific cultural group. [6, 7, 8, 9, 10]

📿 4. Beliefs, Values & Philosophy

Shared moral codes, spiritual guidelines, and existential philosophies are found at the beginning of the DDC system. [6]
  • 100 Philosophy & Psychology: Houses systems of thought, ethics, and values held by specific civilizations.
  • 170 Ethics: Cultural moral values, notions of honor, and community duties.
  • 200 Religion: Spiritual beliefs, mythologies, and religious practices. [6, 8, 10]

📜 5. Heritage & Legacy

The physical and historical tracking of a culture's legacy is found in the final main class. [6]
  • 900 History & Geography: The overarching home for historical accounts of a people.
  • 930–990 History of the Specific World Areas: Books documenting the tangible heritage, archeology, and chronological timeline of specific ethnic groups or nations. [4, 6, 11]
Are you trying to catalog a specific collection of books, or do you need help finding the exact decimal numbers for a particular country or ethnic group's culture?

                                        - kernel (bzImage) and its modules (initramfs.img) are inside rootAVD

        InstallPrebuiltKernelModules    download and install an AOSP prebuilt kernel and its modules into ramdisk.img
                                        - similar to InstallKernelModules, but the AVD needs to be online

Options are exclusive, only one at the time will be processed.

title: Science and Technology
content:
Science and Technology (S&T) is structured into primary branches, sub-branches, and specialized domains.

1. Natural Sciences

Studies the physical world and universe through empirical observation.

  • Physical Sciences
    • Physics: Classical Mechanics, Quantum Mechanics, Thermodynamics, Electromagnetism, Optics, Relativity, Astrophysics, Particle Physics.
    • Chemistry: Organic, Inorganic, Physical, Analytical, Biochemistry, Polymer Chemistry, Theoretical Chemistry.
    • Astronomy & Space Science: Cosmology, Planetary Science, Stellar Astronomy, Astrobiology, Observational Astronomy.
  • Earth & Environmental Sciences
    • Geology: Petrology, Stratigraphy, Volcanology, Seismology, Geomorphology.
    • Meteorology & Atmospheric Science: Climatology, Atmospheric Physics, Paleoclimatology.
    • Oceanography: Physical, Chemical, Biological, and Geological Oceanography.
    • Ecology: Ecosystem Ecology, Conservation Biology, Environmental Science.
  • Life Sciences (Biological Sciences)
    • Cellular & Molecular: Molecular Biology, Genetics, Cytology, Biochemistry.
    • Organismal Biology: Botany (plants), Zoology (animals), Mycology (fungi), Microbiology (bacteria/viruses).
    • Systemic & Evolutionary: Evolutionary Biology, Physiology, Anatomy, Taxonomy, Marine Biology.

2. Formal Sciences

Focuses on abstract concepts, logic, and theoretical structures.

  • Mathematics
    • Pure Mathematics: Algebra, Analysis, Geometry, Topology, Number Theory.
    • Applied Mathematics: Statistics, Probability, Numerical Analysis, Optimization, Financial Mathematics.
  • Computer Science (Theoretical)
    • Algorithms, Data Structures, Computational Complexity, Information Theory, Cryptography.
  • Logic & Systems Theory
    • Mathematical Logic, Set Theory, Systems Science, Game Theory.

3. Social Sciences (Scientific Study of Human Behavior)

Applies scientific methodologies to study individuals and societies.

  • Psychology: Cognitive, Behavioral, Clinical, Neuropsychology, Developmental Psychology.
  • Sociology & Anthropology: Cultural Anthropology, Archeology, Demography, Social Stratification.
  • Economics: Microeconomics, Macroeconomics, Econometrics, Behavioral Economics.
  • Political Science: Comparative Politics, International Relations, Political Economy.

4. Engineering & Applied Technology

Applies scientific and mathematical principles to design and build structures, machines, and systems.

  • Traditional Engineering Fields
    • Civil Engineering: Structural, Transportation, Geotechnical, Environmental Engineering.
    • Mechanical Engineering: Robotics, Mechatronics, Automotive, HVAC, Thermodynamics.
    • Electrical & Electronic Engineering: Power Systems, Microelectronics, Telecommunications, Signal Processing, Photonics.
    • Chemical Engineering: Process Engineering, Biochemical, Materials Science, Petrochemical.
  • Advanced & Interdisciplinary Engineering
    • Aerospace Engineering: Aeronautics, Astronautics, Avionics.
    • Biomedical Engineering: Biomechanics, Tissue Engineering, Medical Instrumentation, Prosthetics.
    • Materials Science: Nanotechnology, Metallurgy, Ceramics, Biomaterials.
    • Industrial & Systems Engineering: Operations Research, Logistics, Ergonomics.

5. Information Technology & Computer Systems

Focuses on computation, software systems, data, and digital infrastructure.

  • Software & Systems
    • Software Engineering, Operating Systems, Systems Architecture, DevOps.
  • Data Science & Artificial Intelligence
    • Machine Learning, Deep Learning, Natural Language Processing (NLP), Computer Vision, Big Data Analytics.
  • Networks & Infrastructure
    • Cybersecurity, Cloud Computing, Distributed Systems, IoT (Internet of Things), Quantum Computing.
  • Digital Interaction
    • Human-Computer Interaction (HCI), Game Development, VR/AR (Extended Reality).

6. Medical & Health Sciences

Focuses on health maintenance, disease prevention, and clinical treatment.

  • Basic Medical Sciences: Human Anatomy, Pathology, Pharmacology, Immunology, Toxicology, Epidemiology.
  • Clinical Medicine: Cardiology, Neurology, Oncology, Pediatrics, Surgery, Psychiatry.
  • Health & Applied Medical Tech: Biomedical Informatics, Public Health, Radiology, Medical Biotechnology, Genetics/Genomics.

7. Agricultural & Bio-Technologies

Applies scientific methods to agriculture, forestry, and food production.

  • Agronomy & Crop Science: Soil Science, Horticulture, Plant Pathology, Precision Agriculture.
  • Animal Science: Livestock Production, Veterinary Medicine, Aquaculture.
  • Food Science & Biotechnology: Food Chemistry, Bioprocess Engineering, Genetic Engineering, Biofuels.

title: Science and Technology
content:
1. Dewey Decimal Classification (DDC)

In the Dewey Decimal System, Science and Technology fall primarily under the 500s (Pure Sciences) and 600s (Applied Sciences/Technology).

500 – Science (Pure Sciences)

  • 500: Science (General, Cybernetics, Systems)
  • 510: Mathematics
  • 520: Astronomy & Allied Sciences
  • 530: Physics
  • 540: Chemistry & Allied Sciences
  • 550: Earth Sciences & Geology
  • 560: Paleontology & Paleozoology
  • 570: Life Sciences & Biology
  • 580: Botanical Sciences (Plants)
  • 590: Zoological Sciences (Animals)

600 – Technology (Applied Sciences)

  • 600: Technology (General)
  • 610: Medicine & Health
  • 620: Engineering & Allied Operations
  • 630: Agriculture & Related Technologies
  • 640: Home & Family Management (Food & Housing Tech)
  • 660: Chemical Engineering & Industrial Chemicals
  • 670: Manufacturing Systems
  • 680: Manufacture for Specific Uses
  • 690: Construction & Building

(Note: Social Sciences under DDC 300 are excluded.)

2. Library of Congress Classification (LCC)

In the Library of Congress system, Science and Technology are split across major letter classes: Q (Science), R (Medicine), S (Agriculture), and T (Technology).

Class Q – Science

  • Q: Science (General)
  • QA: Mathematics & Computer Science
  • QB: Astronomy
  • QC: Physics
  • QD: Chemistry
  • QE: Geology
  • QH: Natural History & Biology (General)
  • QK: Botany
  • QL: Zoology
  • QM: Human Anatomy
  • QP: Physiology
  • QR: Microbiology

Class R – Medicine

  • R: Medicine (General)
  • RA: Public Aspects of Medicine
  • RB: Pathology
  • RC: Internal Medicine & Practice
  • RD: Surgery
  • RE: Ophthalmology
  • RF: Otorhinolaryngology
  • RG: Gynecology & Obstetrics
  • RJ: Pediatrics
  • RK: Dentistry
  • RL: Dermatology
  • RM: Therapeutics & Pharmacology
  • RS: Pharmacy & Materia Medica
  • RT: Nursing
  • RV–RX: Botanic, Homeopathic, & Other Systems

Class S – Agriculture

  • S: Agriculture (General)
  • SB: Plant Culture & Horticulture
  • SD: Forestry
  • SF: Animal Culture & Veterinary Medicine
  • SH: Aquaculture & Fisheries
  • SK: Hunting Sports & Wildlife Management

Class T – Technology

  • T: Technology (General)
  • TA: Engineering (General) & Civil Engineering
  • TC: Hydraulic Engineering
  • TD: Environmental Technology & Sanitary Engineering
  • TE: Highway Engineering
  • TF: Railroad Engineering
  • TG: Bridge Engineering
  • TH: Building Construction
  • TJ: Mechanical Engineering & Machinery
  • TK: Electrical Engineering, Electronics, & Nuclear Engineering
  • TL: Motor Vehicles, Aeronautics, & Astronautics
  • TN: Mining Engineering & Metallurgy
  • TP: Chemical Technology
  • TR: Photography
  • TS: Manufacturing Engineering
  • TT: Handicrafts & Arts and Crafts
  • TX: Home Economics

(Note: Social Sciences under LCC H [Social Sciences], J [Political Science], and K [Law] are excluded.)

Sub ImportFormatAndClean()
    Dim xlApp As Object
    Dim xlWB As Object
    Dim xlSheet As Object
    Dim filePath As String
    Dim startRow As Long, endRow As Long, i As Long
    Dim wordTable As Table
    Dim newRow As Row
    Dim cellTarget As Cell
    Dim titleText As String, authorText As String, publisherText As String
    Dim insertRange As Range
    
    Dim rng As Range
    
    Dim doc As Document
    Dim tbl As Table
    Dim cel As Cell
    Dim wrd As Range
    Dim particleList As Variant
    Dim j As Long
    Dim isParticle As Boolean
    Dim cleanWord As String
    Dim afterColon As Boolean

    ' ==========================================
    ' PHASE 1: Import Excel Rows to Word Table
    ' ==========================================
    
    ' 1. Select the Excel file
    With Application.FileDialog(1)
        .Title = "Select the Excel File"
        .Filters.Clear
        .Filters.Add "Excel Files", "*.xlsx; *.xlsm; *.xls"
        If .Show = -1 Then
            filePath = .SelectedItems(1)
        Else
            Exit Sub
        End If
    End With

    ' 2. Prompt for row range
    On Error Resume Next
    startRow = CLng(InputBox("Enter the STARTING row number in Excel:", "Start Row"))
    endRow = CLng(InputBox("Enter the ENDING row number in Excel:", "End Row"))
    On Error GoTo 0

    If startRow <= 0 Or endRow < startRow Then
        MsgBox "Invalid row range specified.", vbCritical
        Exit Sub
    End If

    ' Freeze screen updating for massive performance boost during processing
    Application.ScreenUpdating = False

    ' 3. Connect to Excel
    On Error Resume Next
    Set xlApp = GetObject(, "Excel.Application")
    If xlApp Is Nothing Then
        Set xlApp = CreateObject("Excel.Application")
    End If
    On Error GoTo 0

    Set xlWB = xlApp.Workbooks.Open(filePath, ReadOnly:=True)
    Set xlSheet = xlWB.Sheets(1)

    ' 4. Reference Word table (Uses ActiveDocument)
    If ActiveDocument.Tables.Count = 0 Then
        Application.ScreenUpdating = True
        MsgBox "No table found in this Word document.", vbCritical
        xlWB.Close False
        Exit Sub
    End If
    Set wordTable = ActiveDocument.Tables(1)

    ' 5. Loop through specified rows
    For i = startRow To endRow
        ' Read and trim raw values from Excel
        titleText = Trim(IIf(IsNull(xlSheet.Cells(i, 1).Value), "", CStr(xlSheet.Cells(i, 1).Value)))
        authorText = Trim(IIf(IsNull(xlSheet.Cells(i, 2).Value), "", CStr(xlSheet.Cells(i, 2).Value)))
        publisherText = Trim(IIf(IsNull(xlSheet.Cells(i, 3).Value), "", CStr(xlSheet.Cells(i, 3).Value)))

        ' --- Punctuation Logic Rules ---
        
        ' Rule A: If Title (Cell 1) ends in a period, remove it
        If Right(titleText, 1) = "." Then
            titleText = Trim(Left(titleText, Len(titleText) - 1))
        End If

        ' Rule B: If Author (Cell 2) does NOT end in a period, add one (only if cell isn't blank)
        If Len(authorText) > 0 Then
            If Right(authorText, 1) <> "." Then
                authorText = authorText & "."
            End If
        End If

        ' Add a new row to the Word table
        Set newRow = wordTable.Rows.Add
        
        ' Target Column 2
        Set cellTarget = newRow.Cells(2)
        cellTarget.Range.Text = "" ' Clear cell

        ' Set up moving range pointer
        Set insertRange = cellTarget.Range
        insertRange.End = insertRange.End - 1 ' Lock inside cell bounds

        ' Insert Title (Underlined & Italicized, period-stripped)
        insertRange.Text = titleText
        insertRange.Font.Underline = wdUnderlineSingle
        insertRange.Font.Italic = True

        ' Advance past the formatted title text
        insertRange.Collapse wdCollapseEnd
        
        ' Insert " / Author Publisher" (Normal format with proper spacing)
        If Len(authorText) > 0 Or Len(publisherText) > 0 Then
            insertRange.Text = " / " & authorText & " " & publisherText
        Else
            insertRange.Text = ""
        End If
        
        insertRange.Font.Underline = wdUnderlineNone
        insertRange.Font.Italic = False
    Next i

    ' Clean up Excel process safely
    xlWB.Close False
    xlApp.Quit
    Set xlSheet = Nothing
    Set xlWB = Nothing
    Set xlApp = Nothing


    ' ==========================================
    ' PHASE 2: Fix Punctuation Spacing
    ' ==========================================
    
    Set rng = ActiveDocument.Content

    ' PART A: Remove any spaces immediately BEFORE colons or semicolons
    With rng.Find
        .ClearFormatting
        .Replacement.ClearFormatting
        .Text = "[ ]@([:;])"
        .Replacement.Text = "\1"
        .Forward = True
        .Wrap = wdFindContinue
        .MatchWildcards = True
        .Execute Replace:=wdReplaceAll
    End With

    ' PART B: Ensure there is exactly ONE space AFTER colons or semicolons
    Set rng = ActiveDocument.Content
    With rng.Find
        .ClearFormatting
        .Replacement.ClearFormatting
        .Text = "([:;])[ ]{1,}"
        .Replacement.Text = "\1 "
        .Forward = True
        .Wrap = wdFindContinue
        .MatchWildcards = True
        .Execute Replace:=wdReplaceAll
    End With

    ' PART C: Insert a space if there are NO spaces after them (e.g., "Word1:Word2")
    Set rng = ActiveDocument.Content
    With rng.Find
        .ClearFormatting
        .Replacement.ClearFormatting
        .Text = "([:;])([a-zA-Z0-9])"
        .Replacement.Text = "\1 \2"
        .Forward = True
        .Wrap = wdFindContinue
        .MatchWildcards = True
        .Execute Replace:=wdReplaceAll
    End With


    ' ==========================================
    ' PHASE 3: Capitalize Underlined Words Except Particles
    ' ==========================================
    
    Set doc = ActiveDocument
    
    ' Comprehensive list of particles
    particleList = Array("a", "an", "the", "and", "but", "or", "nor", "for", "yet", "so", _
                         "as", "if", "that", "than", "because", "though", "while", "unless", _
                         "since", "until", "of", "to", "in", "on", "at", "by", "with", _
                         "from", "up", "out", "off", "over", "down", "through", "into", _
                         "onto", "past", "till", "like", "via", "per", "near")
    
    ' Loop through every table in the document
    For Each tbl In doc.Tables
        ' Loop through every single cell
        For Each cel In tbl.Range.Cells
            afterColon = False
            
            ' Step cleanly word-by-word through the cell
            For Each wrd In cel.Range.Words
                
                ' Check if this specific word is underlined
                If wrd.Font.Underline = wdUnderlineSingle Then
                    
                    ' Isolate the pure word text to evaluate it accurately
                    cleanWord = Trim(wrd.Text)
                    cleanWord = LocalRemovePunctuation(cleanWord)
                    cleanWord = LCase(cleanWord)
                    
                    If Len(cleanWord) > 0 Then
                        isParticle = False
                        
                        ' Check if the word matches your particle criteria
                        For j = LBound(particleList) To UBound(particleList)
                            If cleanWord = particleList(j) Then
                                isParticle = True
                                Exit For
                            End If
                        Next j
                        
                        ' Adjust case adjustments directly on the document
                        If afterColon Or Not isParticle Then
                            wrd.Case = wdTitleWord
                        Else
                            wrd.Case = wdLowerCase
                        End If
                        
                        afterColon = False
                    End If
                End If
                
                ' Flag tracking: check if a colon appears to trigger the next word
                If InStr(wrd.Text, ":") > 0 Then
                    afterColon = True
                End If
            Next wrd
        Next cel
    Next tbl
    
    ' Restore system rendering and alert completion
    Application.ScreenUpdating = True
    MsgBox "All processing, micro-spacing corrections, and title capitalizations are complete!", vbInformation, "Sequence Complete"
End Sub

' Private supporting string-cleaner helper function
Private Function LocalRemovePunctuation(txt As String) As String
    Dim i As Integer
    Dim ch As String
    Dim result As String
    result = ""
    For i = 1 To Len(txt)
        ch = Mid(txt, i, 1)
        If ch Like "[a-zA-Z0-9]" Then
            result = result & ch
        End If
    Next i
    LocalRemovePunctuation = result
End Function
